We have carbon NMR shifts. Need number of carbonyl (C=O) groups. Carbonyl carbons appear around 160-220 ppm for ketones, aldehydes, esters, acids, amides. In the list we have a shift at 160.80 ppm. That's likely a carbonyl carbon (maybe an ester or amide). No other high shifts >150. So likely one carbonyl.

But could also be aromatic carbons around 130-140. 160 could be aromatic carbon attached to electronegative group (e.g., phenyl C attached to O). However typical carbonyl for ester ~170-180, acid ~180-185, amide ~165-175, ketone ~205-215, aldehyde ~190-200. 160.80 is a bit low for carbonyl but could be conjugated carbonyl (e.g., amide). Could also be aromatic C attached to O (e.g., phenoxy). But we need to decide.

We could also get IR to see C=O stretch. Let's request IR.
